entries.topic: Syria: Israeli strike campaigns and civilian tolls, 2013-2026; Sweida 2025

claims.text: SOHR count released 22 July 2025: 1,311 killed in the Sweida violence before the ceasefire: 833 Druze (533 fighters, 300 civilians, of whom 196 'summarily executed' by members of the defence and interior ministries), 423 government forces (including 15 killed in Israeli strikes), 35 Sunni Bedouin (3 civilians executed by Druze fighters). Israel said it struck to protect the Druze.

SOHR annual report (1 Jan 2026): 460 Israeli ground violations documented in southern Syria (Quneitra, Daraa) in 2025, more than 90 ground operations in November; no casualty figure attributed to Israel; 990 civilian deaths in Suwayda in 2025; 2,691 civilians named as killed in 63 massacres 6 Mar-24 Nov 2025 attributed to government-affiliated forces.

Airwars tracks alleged civilian harm from Israeli strikes in Syria from January 2013; its tracker page gives a headline estimate of 60-108 civilians alleged killed, with 6 graded incidents (12-16 locally reported deaths) and the Israeli military's own count 0 civilians; the dataset is graded only in part.

entries.topic: Iran: 2025 and 2026 wars - civilian infrastructure, displacement, Iranian government civilian count

claims.text: UN/OCHA update No. 3 (16 Apr 2026), citing Iranian sources: Ministry of Health counted at least 2,362 civilians killed and 32,314+ injured 28 Feb-7 Apr 2026; about 3.2 million people (800,000 households) relocated inside Iran (government figure, 13-15 Apr), ~60% women and children; UNHCR: ~118,300 crossed to Turkey and Pakistan, mostly routine or precautionary; ~125,600 civilian units damaged incl. ~100,000 residential (IRCS, 10 Apr); 1,000+ electricity distribution points damaged (Ministry of Energy, 6 Apr); 15 bridges, railway sites and 5 fuel tanks damaged (IRCS).

Israeli strike on Tehran's Evin prison, 23 June 2025: Iranian government said 79 killed (relatives, staff, conscripts, a child, residents); Israeli officials called it 'symbolic', Sa'ar a response to Iranian missile fire; HRW (14 Aug 2025) called it 'unlawfully indiscriminate' and an apparent war crime.

entries.topic: Israeli strikes in Iraq (2019) and Yemen (2024-2025) with tolls; Houthi attacks on Israel

claims.text: 2019: a series of explosions at Popular Mobilisation Forces bases and depots in Iraq (Amerli 19 July; Camp Ashraf 27 July; south Baghdad 12 August, one civilian killed and 29 injured; Balad 20 August; al-Qaim 25 August, six killed per the PMF; others in September); Netanyahu on 22 August: 'We are working against Iranian consolidation - in Iraq as well'; Iraq closed its airspace to unauthorised flights on 13 August.

23 Aug 2019: two US officials told AP Israel struck an Iranian weapons depot at a militia base in Amerli on 19 July; Netanyahu: 'I don't give Iran immunity anywhere', security forces have 'a free hand'; PMF deputy head blamed Israeli drones but ultimately Washington.

19 Dec 2024 (Israeli strikes on Hodeidah, Ras Isa, Salif ports and Dhahban and Heyzaz power plants): at least nine killed per Houthi sources; 26 Dec 2024: Sanaa airport control tower and runway, ports and power stations hit while WHO chief Tedros was at the airport (a crew member injured); toll reported from 3-4 (Al-Masirah) to six killed, ~40 wounded (CNN); Israel: retaliation for Houthi missile and drone fire.

2025 Israeli attacks in Yemen: after a Houthi missile hit near Ben Gurion airport on 4 May, strikes on 5 May (4 killed), 6 May (Sanaa airport disabled, 3 killed), 16 May, 28 May (Yemenia's last plane), June-July port strikes, 24 Aug (10 killed, 102 wounded, Houthi ministry), 28 Aug (PM al-Rahawi and ministers killed), ~10 Sept, 16 Sept Hodeidah, ~25 Sept (8 killed, 142 injured, BBC); an Eilat drone injured 22 before late-Sept strikes; page total 61+ killed, 463+ injured; Houthis confirmed chief of staff al-Ghamari's death from the June strike on 16 Oct 2025.
10 Sept 2025 Israeli strikes on Sanaa and al-Jawf: Houthi-run Health Ministry 46 killed, 165 wounded (AP, 11 Sept); Israel: response to Houthi drones and missiles.
Netanyahu tied the 10 Sept 2025 strikes to a Houthi drone that hit Ramon airport's arrivals hall; Saba (Houthi) gave 35 killed, 131 wounded at first.

CPJ: the 10 Sept 2025 strike on the 26 September and al-Yemen newspaper offices in Sanaa killed 31 journalists and media workers, including a child; IDF said it hit the 'Houthi Public Relations Department'; CPJ classed the killings as murders, the deadliest attack on the press it had recorded in 16 years.

entries.topic: Egypt and Jordan: Rafah, displacement red lines, economic effects, treaty strains; Gaza displacement

claims.text: Sisi, Cairo, 29 Jan 2025: displacement of Gazans an 'injustice that we cannot take part in'; it 'can never be tolerated or allowed because of its impact on Egyptian national security'; came after Trump's 25 Jan call to 'clean out' Gaza; King Abdullah II reaffirmed keeping Palestinians on their land.
Sisi, 7 Apr 2025: Red Sea tension cost Egypt about $7 billion in Suez Canal revenue in 2024 (his figure, not independently verified).

Netanyahu approved on 17 Dec 2025 a Leviathan gas export deal worth about 112bn shekels (~$35bn), 'the largest gas deal in Israel's history'; in Sept 2025 he had ordered it held after Israeli allegations that Egypt's Sinai deployments violated the peace treaty, which Egypt denies; Egypt's SIS (Rashwan): 'a purely commercial transaction' with 'no political dimensions'.

Israel seized the Rafah crossing in May 2024; COGAT announced reopening for people from 1 Feb 2026 after the last hostage's body was recovered; returns limited to those who left during the war, 'only after prior security clearance by Israel', coordinated with Egypt.
Rafah, reopened in early Feb 2026, closed again after the US-Israeli war on Iran began; Israeli authorities said it would reopen on 18 March 2026 for 'limited movement of people'.

MEI (7 Oct 2026): Iran launched more than 250 missiles and drones at Jordan in 2026, mainly at the US presence and Aqaba, most intercepted, minimal damage; no Jordanian casualties reported; visitors H1 2026 fell to 3.1m; Israeli gas imports suspended at the start of the war, raising power costs ~$140m a month; tourism 14-16% of GDP.
IMF (Feb 2024): Jordan growth projected ~2.6% for 2024, down from 3%; hotel occupancy fell ~32% in the first week of Dec 2023 year on year; lower travel receipts.
UNRWA sitrep 64 (15 Jan 2024): 'up to 1.9 million people (or over 85 per cent of the population) have been displaced across the Gaza Strip, some multiple times'.

claims.text: Houthi-run health ministry's later update on the 20 July 2024 Israeli strike on Hodeidah: 'at least three people were killed and 87 injured'; an earlier statement gave 80 wounded and no deaths.

IBTimes UK, 16 Oct 2026: the Pentagon's Minab report remained unpublished; a Pentagon spokesperson said the investigation was ongoing; anonymous sources (via The Straits Times) said officials intended to delay release until after the midterms; a Bloomberg investigation gave more than 150 killed incl. at least 123 children; a UN fact-finding mission report of 17 Sept 2026 found reasonable grounds to believe the US was responsible and that the strike was an indiscriminate attack amounting to a war crime.

27 May 2024: one Egyptian member of the security personnel near the Rafah border was killed in an exchange of fire with Israeli personnel; both Egypt's military and Israel's military said they were investigating.

AP via Al Jazeera, 23 Aug 2019: two US officials said the 19 July 2019 Amerli raid, on a base a militia official said housed Iranian and Lebanese advisers and a weapons depot, was Israeli and killed two Iranian military commanders.

CPJ: 31 journalists and media support workers killed on 10 Sept 2025 (at least nine confirmed as journalists, others under investigation), plus a child; CPJ classifies the deaths as murders; the IDF said it struck military targets including the 'Houthi Public Relations Department', which it said disseminates propaganda.
Airwars tracker: 60-108 civilians alleged killed in Syria by Israeli strikes; 6 alleged incidents with 12-16 locally reported deaths; IDF estimate 0 civilian deaths from 1 incident.
